introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2020. Duration: two and a half hours. Do ALL the tasks (Task 1, Task 2 and Task 3) specified in the question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two and Group Three. Each version has three tasks: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task 3 (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks).

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (the pictures 'foxandstork' and 'hareandtortoise' found on the desktop) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

Transcrites en neuf fichiers : numero_exercice G1-T1, G1-T2, G1-T3, G2-T1, ..., G3-T3 ; groupes ["GROUP 1"], ["GROUP 2"] ou ["GROUP 3"]. Rien n'est imprimé sur le fait qu'un candidat ne traite qu'une seule version : regles_choix reste vide (convention des Paper 3 de pratique).

Les filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo, les cadres d'en-tête (numero de centre, nom du candidat, « For examiners' use only »), les lignes à compléter, la réponse manuscrite « Microsoft office Word 2007 » portée à la main sur la page 2 et les artefacts de scanner sont ignores. Les images « foxandstork » et « hareandtortoise » et les fichiers du bureau ne figurent pas dans le PDF.

Aucun logiciel (Word, Excel, compilateur C ou Pascal) n'a été exécuté : les menus et les étapes sont donnés de mémoire (Office récent) et ne sont pas testés. Les formules de tableur ont été traduites en Python et exécutées sur les données du sujet (COUNT, COUNTA, ROUND, AVERAGE, RANK, COUNTIF). Le code C et Pascal n'a pas été compilé : sa logique a été vérifiée par une simulation Python fidèle (mêmes entrées, mêmes sorties, cas limites).
Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : les réponses sont rédigées. Les répartitions de points dans les corrigés (quand il y en a) sont indicatives ; les points imprimés du sujet ne sont jamais modifiés.

Task 2, Group Three : points imprimés 5 + (2+1+2+1) + 2 + 3 + 4 = 20 ; sur le scan, les marques de la question 2 sont lues 2, 1, 2, 1 pour a, b, c, d ; la question 3 (2 marks) couvre B9 et la copie. Figure 2 recadrée sans filigrane depuis la page 13 : la bande grise des en-têtes de colonnes (A à F) est texturée sur le scan d'origine (c'est la capture d'écran, pas un filigrane) ; les valeurs sont lisibles. Le sujet ne précise pas le format des cellules « with formatting » : bordures, chiffres en italique et heures h:mm lus sur la figure. Moyennes recalculées par Python : 37.55, 38.2333, 38.9333, 38.5167, 37.3667. Le sujet demande un « pie chart » de températures, peu significatif (pas de parties d'un tout) : traité tel quel.

questions.enonce_markdown: Create a workbook called Task 2 and enter the worksheet data as provided with formatting.  *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Start a blank workbook and type the data of Figure 2:

- row **1** (A1 to F1): `Time`, `Monday`, `Tuesday`, `Wednesday`, `Thursday`, `Friday`;
- column **A** (A2 to A7): the times `4:00`, `8:00`, `12:00`, `16:00`, `20:00`, `0:00` (typed as times, format *h:mm*);
- columns **B to F**, rows 2 to 7: the temperatures of the figure, each day in its own column.

| Time | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4:00 | 38 | 38.2 | 38.6 | 39.1 | 37.8 |
| 8:00 | 37.3 | 38.3 | 38.7 | 38.8 | 37.6 |
| 12:00 | 37 | 38 | 38.8 | 38.6 | 37.4 |
| 16:00 | 37.4 | 38.1 | 39 | 38.4 | 37.4 |
| 20:00 | 37.6 | 38.3 | 39.1 | 38.2 | 37.2 |
| 0:00 | 38 | 38.5 | 39.4 | 38 | 36.8 |

"With formatting" means keeping the layout of the figure: the cell borders and the italic figures. Save the file under the name **Task 2** (see question 6).

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the data and create a Line Chart for the various days and times.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the data **A1:F7** and open the *Insert* tab > **Insert Line or Area Chart** > **Line** (or *Line with Markers*). Each day is one line (one series) and the times are on the horizontal axis. If the program draws the *Time* column as a sixth line, open *Select Data*, remove the series *Time* and set the times **A2:A7** as the *Horizontal (Category) Axis Labels*.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert chart title as Temperature Variations.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Click the chart, then *Chart Design* > **Add Chart Element** > **Chart Title** > *Above Chart* (or click the title box) and type **Temperature Variations**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Add chart Axis titles as Temperature (degree Celsius) and Time (Hours).  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: *Chart Design* > **Add Chart Element** > **Axis Titles**. In the *Primary Vertical* title type **Temperature (degree Celsius)** and in the *Primary Horizontal* title type **Time (Hours)**. The temperature is on the vertical axis and the time on the horizontal axis.

questions.enonce_markdown: Displace the chart legend to the right of the chart.  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: *Chart Design* > **Add Chart Element** > **Legend** > **Right** (or right-click the legend > *Format Legend* > *Legend Position* > *Right*). The legend, which names the five days, is now at the right of the chart.

questions.enonce_markdown: Use a spreadsheet formula in cell B9 to calculate the average temperature for Monday. Copy the formula across to the other days.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click **B9** and type `=AVERAGE(B2:B7)`. This averages the six readings of Monday: $(38 + 37.3 + 37 + 37.4 + 37.6 + 38) / 6 = 225.3 / 6 = 37.55$. Select B9 and drag the fill handle to the right up to **F9**: the range moves with the column (C2:C7, D2:D7, ...). Results (Python simulation, rounded to 2 decimal places):

| Day | Cell | Average temperature (degree Celsius) |
|---|---|---|
| Monday | B9 | 37.55 |
| Tuesday | C9 | 38.23 |
| Wednesday | D9 | 38.93 |
| Thursday | E9 | 38.52 |
| Friday | F9 | 37.37 |

(Type `Average` in cell A9 as a label if you wish; it is not requested.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Create a bar chart for the average daily temperatures and label the axes.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the day names **B1:F1**, then hold *Ctrl* and select the averages **B9:F9**. *Insert* tab > **Insert Column or Bar Chart** > **Clustered Column** (or *Clustered Bar*). Label the axes: *Chart Design* > *Add Chart Element* > *Axis Titles*, for example **Day** on the horizontal axis and **Average temperature (degree Celsius)** on the vertical axis. Add a chart title if you wish. The bars are about 37.55, 38.23, 38.93, 38.52 and 37.37, the Wednesday bar being the highest.

questions.enonce_markdown: Create a pie chart of days versus the average daily temperatures.  *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: With the same selection (**B1:F1** and **B9:F9**) choose *Insert* > **Insert Pie or Doughnut Chart** > **Pie**. Show the days by keeping the legend (or *Add Chart Element* > *Data Labels* > *Category Name*) and, if you wish, add the values as data labels and a chart title. Each slice represents one day and its size is proportional to that day's average temperature. (A pie chart is meant for parts of a whole; here it simply compares the five averages.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task 2 in your working directory and print a copy.
questions.corrige_markdown: *File* > **Save As** > working directory, file name **Task 2**, then *Save*; then *File* > **Print** and collect the copy.
